preceding_messages.text: I adopt the peg-retirement-on-sustained-obstruction rule and the "OBSOLETE — ACCESS UNRESOLVED" retirement annotation verbatim; they give the indefinite conservative span a defined structural exit without requiring access that may never come. Because your age-based retirement criterion leaves open triggers raised *during* the obstruction period whose physical context has vanished by the time access resumes, I mandate that every queued inter-site trigger carry a three-field context tag—obstruction type, estimated departure condition, and the week-number at which the transient was last physically confirmed present at the site—logged by the original observer at the moment of queuing. The failure this closes: during month two of the fence period a weekly construction-equipment delivery truck parked at Site 3's northern edge trips the 0.5 hPa inter-site spread, the trigger is queued with the truck present, but by month five when access resumes the delivery schedule has ended and the trigger—being younger than the new-site's first NIST cross-check—executes an immediate elevation-recording audit against a coordinate where no truck, no crane, and no transient of any kind remains, dispatching a crew to verify a vanished artifact and printing an appendix entry a year-two resident reads as procedural incoherence. I therefore require that upon access resumption the compiler cross-references each queued trigger's context tag against the current horizon-sketch photograph; if the tagged obstruction is absent from that photograph the trigger is retired under the same "OBSOLETE — ACCESS UNRESOLVED" annotation with the added tag "CONTEXT LAPSAT ACCESS" rather than executed, so the audit trail records that the transient departed before the crew could reach the site rather than that the crew was sent and found nothing.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the three-field context tag, the access-resumption cross-reference, and the "CONTEXT LAPSED AT ACCESS" retirement annotation verbatim; they close the vanished-transient dispatch hole by making the audit trail record the obstruction's departure rather than the crew's futile arrival. Because a single-photograph present/absent test has the temporal resolution of one instant, I mandate that the access-resumption observer update the context tag's departure-estimate field with a current on-site assessment and that any trigger whose updated estimate places departure within 48 hours of the scheduled crew-arrival window is held under a bold "CONTEXT TRANSIENT — DEPARTURE IMMINENT" annotation pending a second confirmation photograph taken no more than six hours before dispatch. The concrete failure this closes: during month-five's access-resumption photograph a recurring weekly delivery truck sits at Site 3's northern edge, the context tag matches, and the trigger executes an immediate elevation-recording audit dispatched for 14:00; the truck completes its delivery at 11:00 and departs, so the crew arrives to find no transient, the apparatus already vacated, and an appendix entry that reads as a verification failure rather than a context lapse.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the 48-hour departure-imminent hold and the six-hour confirmation photograph verbatim; they give the single-instant present/absent test a temporal guard for the immediate dispatch question. For any context tag encoding a recurrence pattern—two or more observed cycles with a logged day-of-week and time-of-day window—the six-hour confirmation is structurally insufficient because the periodic departure can fall between the confirmation instant and the scheduled crew arrival, so I mandate that dispatch confirmation for such tags occur no more than two hours before the logged departure time, and any crew whose assigned arrival falls after that departure retires the trigger under a bold "CONTEXT PERIODIC — DISPATCH WINDOW MISSED" annotation with the next-feasible-cycle date logged in the retirement note. The failure this closes: a weekly Tuesday-morning delivery truck (06:00–09:00) trips the inter-site spread during week 8 of the fence period, the Wednesday access-resumption photograph shows the truck absent and places next departure six days away—well outside your 48-hour window—so the trigger proceeds to normal scheduling; the crew calendar assigns the elevation-recording audit to a Tuesday at 10:00, the truck departs at 09:00, and the appendix prints an entry indistinguishable from a verification failure. I therefore require that the dispatch scheduler, at the moment of crew assignment rather than at access resumption, cross-reference the periodicity field against the assigned arrival time and either confirm an in-window dispatch or execute the retirement with the cycle-date tag, so a year-two appendix reader sees the institution attempting to verify within the transient's present window rather than dispatching blindly into its absence.
